title: Senior's toolkit: relationships, loading and delete rules
summary: Include and its variants, safe delete behaviour, the change tracker view, and scaffolding a model from an existing database.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: relationships, loading and delete rules
steps.body: Related data is where EF Core code goes wrong in production: too much loaded, too little loaded, or a delete that takes half the database with it. These are the tools experienced developers use to stay in control.

toolkit.what: Load related rows in the same query. `ThenInclude` goes one level deeper from the last `Include`.
flags: the string form, handy when the path is built at run time

toolkit.what: A filtered Include: load only the children you need, such as the five newest published posts per blog.
flags: limit how many come back per parent

toolkit.what: Send one SQL query per included collection instead of one big JOIN. Use it when two collection Includes multiply rows (the Cartesian explosion).
flags: force one query when split is the default

toolkit.what: Choose what happens to dependants when a principal is deleted. Required relationships cascade by default; for important data, make deletes fail instead.
flags: delete the children too (default when the FK is required)
refuse the delete while children exist
keep children, clear their FK (FK must be nullable)

toolkit.what: Every tracked entity with its state, keys, property values and navigations. Shows exactly what `SaveChanges` is about to do.
flags: one line per entity: type, key, state
toolkit.when: a related row was saved, deleted or left out unexpectedly

toolkit.what: Generate entities and a context from an existing database (database-first). The usual start when EF Core meets a legacy schema.
flags: overwrite files from a previous scaffold
toolkit.example: dotnet ef dbcontext scaffold "Data Source=legacy.db" Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Sqlite --output-dir Models --context LegacyDb --table Orders --table Customers

steps.prompt: An order page got slow. The log shows one query returning 12,000 rows for an order with 40 lines and 300 audit entries. What is happening, and what do you try first?
options: Two collection Includes in one JOIN multiply rows (40 x 300); add `.AsSplitQuery()` or load the audit entries only when they are needed
The database is missing an index on `Orders.Id`
`Single` loads every order in the table
EF Core always returns 12,000 rows for Include
steps.explain: One JOIN with two collections returns one row per combination: 40 x 300 = 12,000. Split queries send one query per collection, so 1 + 40 + 300 rows come back. Also ask whether the page needs the audit entries at all.

steps.prompt: Match each delete behaviour to what happens when the customer is deleted.
pairs: the delete fails while orders exist
orders stay, with `CustomerId` set to null

steps.prompt: Load each blog with only its five newest published posts and each post's author.
You must start using EF Core against an existing legacy database. Put the steps in order.
lines: dotnet ef dbcontext scaffold "Data Source=legacy.db" Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Sqlite --output-dir Models --context LegacyDb
Read the generated entities and fix names and relationships in partial classes
Write a query and check it with ToQueryString()

items: Which entities are Added or Modified right now?
Does this Include become one JOIN or several queries?
What SQL does the filtered Include send?
Get entity classes for a 200-table database that already exists

steps.title: Make it a habit
steps.body: Before merging a query with more than one collection Include, read its SQL and count the rows it returns. Set `OnDelete` on purpose for every relationship that holds money or history, and print `ChangeTracker.DebugView.LongView` whenever `SaveChanges` does something you did not ask for.
